summary: tldr reaching-defs on real rust functions returned `definitions: 0` and empty gen/kill/in/out for every block, regardless of body content. Root cause: the rust DFG extractor (process_rust_let + extract_refs_from_node dispatch in crates/tldr-core/src/dfg/extractor.rs) only recognised `identifier`, `mut_pattern`, and `tuple_pattern` as let-binding shapes, and did not dispatch the `let_condition` AST node at all. Real rust code overwhelmingly uses `tuple_struct_pattern` (`Some(c)`, `Ok(v)`, `Err(_)`), `reference_pattern` (`&x`, `&mut y`), `or_pattern`, and `struct_pattern` in let bindings, AND `let_condition` is the node that wraps the `let pat = expr` form inside `while let`, `if let`, and the 2024-edition `let_chain`. Fixed by routing both `let_declaration` and `let_condition` through a new recursive `extract_rust_binding_identifiers` walker that handles all canonical pattern kinds.

bug_status.C2: FIXED — rust reaching-defs now emits gen/kill/in/out per block when the body contains any let_declaration / let_condition / for_expression binding (tuple_struct_pattern, reference_pattern, or_pattern, struct_pattern, mut_pattern, tuple_pattern, identifier).
bug_status.C3: DEFERRED with explanation — the audit assertion `available reports function name not null` does not match the AvailableExprsInfo struct shape: there is no `function` field in the JSON for ANY language (python, rust, c all return the same key set: avail_in/avail_out/all_exprs/entry_block/uncertain_exprs/confidence). The user-visible symptom that the audit likely meant — `low confidence` on rust — comes from the text-based `detect_uncertain_expression` (crates/tldr-core/src/dataflow/available.rs:957) which flags any line containing `= ... fn_call(...) + ...` as uncertain. This is language-agnostic; python flask::make_response shows the same `confidence=low` with all_exprs=5 / uncertain=37. Fixing C2 (rust DFG defs) does NOT change the rust available confidence because uncertain detection runs on source text, not on refs. A proper C3 fix would require either (a) language-aware purity inference for callees, or (b) reweighting compute_confidence to ignore uncertain_exprs when at least one binary_expression was confirmed — both larger structural changes outside this milestone's scope. Per task scope guardrail (`fix the smaller one fully and commit; defer the bigger one with a TODO`), C3 is left to a future milestone; the regression test `rust_available_function_name_not_null` guards the analysis-runs-and-returns-data invariant so a regression to truly null output would still be caught.

fix_summary:
Two changes in crates/tldr-core/src/dfg/extractor.rs:
  1. `extract_refs_from_node` now matches `"let_declaration" | "let_condition"` for the rust binding-statement form (was: only `"let_declaration"`). This catches `while let Some(c) = ...` and `if let Ok(v) = ...`.
  2. `process_rust_let` and `process_rust_for` delegate the pattern walk to a new `extract_rust_binding_identifiers` recursive helper. The helper kind-dispatches on identifier / mut_pattern / tuple_pattern / tuple_struct_pattern / reference_pattern / or_pattern / struct_pattern, with the constructor-vs-binding split inside `tuple_struct_pattern` (first named child is the ctor, subsequent named children are bindings) and the field-vs-binding split inside `struct_pattern::field_pattern` (shorthand `{ y }` makes the field its own binding; `{ field: pat }` recurses into pat). `process_rust_let` also visits the let-else `block` child so divergent branches with their own statements are walked.

scope_decisions: Did NOT touch crates/tldr-core/src/dfg/reaching.rs — the gen/kill computation is correct; the bug was purely upstream in the refs extractor.
Did NOT touch crates/tldr-core/src/dataflow/available.rs — see deferred_c3 note above.

Did NOT add a generic language-agnostic pattern visitor; stayed inside the rust arm. The new `extract_rust_binding_identifiers` lives next to `process_rust_let` and only `match`es rust AST node kinds.
Did NOT migrate process_rust_for off its old inline pattern handling beyond making it call the new helper — kept the change surgical.
